title: Provision-on-demand control-plane fabric: Terraform module for private EKS control plane lifecycle
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Author a composable Terraform module that provisions a production-grade private EKS control plane and surrounding lifecycle plumbing as a reusable 'provision-on-demand' fabric. This module should enable idempotent cluster creation, safe minor-version upgrades of the control plane, automated preflight validations, health probes surfaceable to Redwood Console, and an automated rollback path for failed upgrades. The module must be suitable for hosted Dedicated/Private installs (VPCed control plane endpoints), integrate with our KMS and cross-account key policies, and expose outputs for Dedicated autoscaling/orchestration layers to consume. Key differentiators versus existing provisioners: (1) explicit canary-less staged upgrade flow using ephemeral control-plane isolates for preflight, (2) composable child modules for VPC / IAM / KMS / control-plane / rotation / health with clear interfaces, (3) built-in health and repair signals that map to Console SLOs and incident runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module lives under modules/control-plane/provision-on-demand and follows Redwood module styleguide
Module can create a private EKS cluster control plane (private endpoint) with required IAM and KMS bindings using only provided inputs
Idempotent applies: re-running with same inputs results in no drift and no destructive changes unless version bump is requested
Preflight hook: terraform apply triggers an isolated ephemeral canary-control-plane (short lived) that runs smoke tests and API-level checks before allowing production control-plane upgrade
Health signals: control plane health exporter and CloudWatch alarms exist and forward to Console metrics with token/route mapping
Upgrade rollback: if preflight or health checks fail post-upgrade, module exposes a documented rollback path and can re-surface previous kubeconfig/manifest snapshot
Automated integration tests in CI can provision and destroy a cluster in under 45 minutes with no manual steps
tech_notes: Implementation pattern: root module composes stable child modules: vpc, kms, iam, eks-controlplane, rotation, preflight, health-exporter
Terraform target: >= 1.5, use CLI-driven apply in CI with state in S3 + DynamoDB locking; support backend override for on-prem customers
Avoid use of local-exec remote-provisioner where possible; prefer provider-native resources and null_resource only for last-resort integration hooks
Preflight flow: create ephemeral control-plane with minimal worker profile + run conformance and e2e smoke scripts; TTL tag triggers automated destroy; results gate promotion of version change

Upgrade strategy: minor-version bump staged as: create ephemeral preflight cluster -> run smoke tests -> apply control-plane upgrade in prod cluster with slow drift guard and post-upgrade health window -> monitor 30m; if health regression detected, trigger documented rollback
Health: deploy lightweight control-plane exporter (Lambda with cross-account role) that polls EKS DescribeCluster API, KV cache latency, etc; integrate with Console via metrics exporter endpoint
KMS: module supports customer-managed keys and cross-account grants; keys rotated on schedule with annotations for audit logs
Outputs: kubeconfig_secret_arn, control_plane_endpoint_private, cluster_version, health_exporter_endpoint, preflight_artifact_bucket
Testing: add terratest suites and a fast-mode integration test run for CI that uses smaller instance types and reduced timeouts
Observability: emit structured events to Console Rollout API (canary_start, canary_pass, canary_fail, upgrade_complete, upgrade_rollback)

Pay attention to permission scoping for health-exporter role and KMS grant lifetime settings
Verify outputs are minimal and stable (avoid leaking ARNs that change across applies)
